title: Technical Architecture Blueprint Completed
author: NSW Team
excerpt: The project team completed the NSW technical architecture blueprint, defining the system design, ASYCUDA World integration, and security measures.
content: The National Single Window (NSW) technical team announced the completion of the technical architecture blueprint on May 15, 2025. This key document defines the overall system design, core components, and their interoperability, establishing the technical foundation for the software development phase.

The proposed architecture is based on a modular microservices approach, enabling scalability and ease of maintenance. One of the most critical aspects is the tight integration with the ASYCUDA World system, currently used by the General Directorate of Customs for managing customs declarations.

Data security and information protection occupy a central place in the proposed architecture. The system will employ advanced encryption, multi-factor authentication, and a comprehensive audit trail of all actions. These measures ensure compliance with international cybersecurity standards.

The blueprint also includes detailed specifications for the application programming interfaces (APIs) that will be used for communication between the NSW and the systems of the eight cross-border regulatory agencies. UN/CEFACT standards have been used as the basis for the data model.
The next step will be the commencement of the software development phase, which is expected to begin in the third quarter of 2025, following final approval from the project Steering Committee.
